items.title: FDA clears Elucid FFR-IQ: AI FFR-CT software that adds plaque composition to coronary physiology estimates
items.summary: On October 21, 2026, Elucid announced FDA 510(k) clearance of FFR-IQ, AI software that estimates fractional flow reserve noninvasively from coronary CT angiography by combining coronary anatomy with plaque composition.
bullets: FFR-IQ estimates FFR from a standard CCTA, using invasive pressure-wire FFR as the reference standard, to help decide which patients need invasive angiography and revascularization.
Unlike anatomy-only FFR-CT, it feeds plaque burden and composition (including lipid-rich necrotic core, from the company's Plaque-IQ software) into the physiology estimate.

The company reports 92.2% sensitivity and 93.1% specificity in the ELUCIDATE FFR-CT study that supported the clearance (FDA 510(k) K262015, dated Sept 29, 2026); full results are due at TCT 2026 on November 1 and are not yet peer-reviewed.

Take-home: noninvasive coronary physiology is moving toward combined anatomy-plaque-flow assessment from one CT scan; wait for the ELUCIDATE data before judging how it compares with existing FFR-CT tools.
items.source: Elucid press release via Business Wire (Oct 21, 2026)
